artifacts.synopsis: TE David Senters complained that Savannah River Presbytery erred by judging TE Stamberg's stated difference with WCF 21.3 regarding the gift of tongues as 'not a difference' during a transfer examination. The SJC denied the procedural part of the complaint but sustained the confessional part, finding it was error to conclude Stamberg's view on continuing tongues was not a difference with WCF 1.1 and 1.6, and remanded to Presbytery for further action.

artifacts.synopsis: Complainants challenged Mississippi Valley Presbytery's approval of James Blaha's theological examination for ordination regarding his views on charismatic gifts. The Special Judicial Commission upheld the challenge regarding prophecy (finding Blaha's views allow possibility of continuing revelation contrary to WCF 1.1 and 6), but rejected the challenge regarding tongues (finding private prayer language use within bounds of 1974 Pastoral Letter). Commission ordered presbytery to note prophecy exception in minutes and instruct Blaha not to teach or preach this view.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Robert Hopper challenged James River Presbytery's restriction on teaching and preaching about present-day prophecy and tongues. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that presbytery may limit such teaching for the welfare of the church when it determines the views threaten the church's peace or purity, while declining to issue a comprehensive doctrinal ruling.
